gap: No result ChatGPT got states which device each built-in cable can bring to its top charging tier: Apple requires AVS and USB-PD 3.2 at 60 W or more for iPhone 18 Pro, ChargerLAB's readout of the UGREEN 100W cable shows PD 3.0/PPS and no AVS, the ESR Xtend 45W is the only retractable charger read with a named AVS claim, and the only cable read above 100 W is the UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W's (140 W per Android Central and Notebookcheck).
standout_why: Compared against UGREEN's US retractable landing page (names and prices only, no cable watts or protocols), both Belkin support articles (67 W, PD/PPS, no AVS mention, no phone or laptop tier), and ChargerLAB's teardown (lists the cable's protocols but ties them to no device and does not mention AVS). None maps a cable to Apple's iPhone 18 Pro or MacBook fast-charge requirements, and none gives the 160W model's cable watts. The Verge page would not open, and us.ugreen.com and esrtech.com product pages returned HTTP 429 on every attempt, so the UGREEN 100W product page was not compared.
decides: It splits the pick by device instead of crowning the UGREEN 100W for everyone. For an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max, the ESR Xtend 45W (ours) is the only one read with an AVS claim; ChargerLAB's readout of the UGREEN 100W cable shows no AVS, so by Apple's rule that cable does not give that phone its top tier. For a 14-inch MacBook Pro, the UGREEN 100W cable (ours) is the lowest-priced one read that clears Apple's 96 W fast-charge line; the 60–67 W cables do not. For a 16-inch MacBook Pro (Nov 2023 or later), only the UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W's cable reaches 140 W, so ChatGPT's 'strongest verified option' is not the top-wattage cable. UGREEN is a partner store, but the 160W has no Dealectric record yet.

findings.label: What an iPhone 18 Pro / Pro Max needs for its top wired speed
findings.value: Apple 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max, or a third-party adapter of 60 W or higher that uses Adjustable Voltage Supply (AVS) and supports USB-PD 3.2; about 50% in around 15 minutes
findings.source_title: Apple Support: Fast charge your iPhone
findings.note: Same page: iPhone 17, 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max need a 40 W or higher adapter (50% in around 20 minutes); iPhone Air and 17e need 20 W or higher. Apple's times are its own lab results. Page was read through a summarising fetch; requirement wording is partly quoted, partly paraphrased.

findings.product: UGREEN Nexode 100W Charger with Retractable USB-C Cable (X606)
findings.label: Protocols ChargerLAB detected on the built-in cable
findings.value: UFCS, QC3+, PD 3.0/PPS, DCP, Samsung 5V/2A, Apple 2.4A; fixed 5/9/12/15 V at 3 A and 20 V at 5 A (100 W); PPS 5–21 V at up to 5 A; no AVS in the readout
findings.source_title: Teardown of the UGREEN Nexode 100W Charger with Retractable USB-C Cable - ChargerLAB
findings.note: Measured by ChargerLAB with a POWER-Z KM003C; model X606, part number 65591. The article does not mention AVS; 'no AVS' is absence from the detected list, not a ChargerLAB statement. Set against Apple's rule above, this cable does not meet the iPhone 18 Pro's 60 W AVS / PD 3.2 requirement.

findings.source_title: Teardown of the UGREEN Nexode 100W Charger with Retractable USB-C Cable - ChargerLAB
findings.note: ChargerLAB protocol readout. A phone that fast-charges only over Huawei SCP/FCP or Samsung AFC would have to use a port with its own cable, not the built-in one. USB-C2 tops out at 30 W (20 V/1.5 A) with PPS 5–11 V at 2.75 A; USB-A 22.5 W.

findings.label: Which built-in cable wattage fast-charges which MacBook, per Apple's adapter list
findings.value: 16-inch MacBook Pro (2021 or later): 140 W only, and over a USB-C charge cable only on the Nov 2023 or later models. 14-inch MacBook Pro (2021 or later): 96 W or 140 W. MacBook Air (2022 or later): 70 W, 96 W or 140 W; 67 W on 13.6-inch models only
findings.source_title: Apple Support: Fast charge your MacBook Air or MacBook Pro
findings.note: Apple lists its own adapters; applying the wattage lines to third-party chargers is our inference. A built-in USB-C cable cannot be MagSafe 3, so a 2021 or early-2023 16-inch MacBook Pro has no fast-charge pairing on Apple's list from any retractable charger. A 60 W cable (UGREEN 65W) sits under every MacBook line; 67 W cables (Belkin, Baseus) reach only the 13.6-inch Air line; 100 W clears the 14-inch Pro line; only 140 W clears the 16-inch line.

findings.label: AVS and 60 W claim, named reviewer
findings.value: rated 45 W; 'supports up to 60W dynamic charging with AVS', which the reviewer says unlocks the fastest charge speeds on iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max; built-in cable up to 3.1 ft; one extra USB-C port
findings.source_title: Hands-on: ESR's 45W Xtend charger is an excellent iPhone fast charger on the go - 9to5Mac
findings.note: Michael Burkhardt, 1 Nov 2026. Hands-on, not a lab measurement. The article does not say whether the 60 W mode is on the built-in cable, the port or both, and does not mention PD 3.2. It quotes $49.99 regular, $35.99 (white) and $41.99 (burgundy) on Amazon as of 1 Nov; those are not today's prices.

findings.label: ESR's support page: output and stated limits
findings.value: 'supports 5–20V and up to 3A, with a maximum total output of 45W when both ports are in use'; power is split automatically between two devices; 'some OPPO and Huawei phones support only proprietary charging protocols' and may charge slowly or not at all; for full speed the device should need 45 W or less with nothing in the other USB-C port
findings.source_title: ESR Xtend 45W Retractable Charger - ESR Help
findings.note: ESR's own troubleshooting page. It does not state the 60 W figure, an AVS voltage range or a per-output split; 20 V × 3 A = 60 W is consistent with the claim but is our arithmetic, not ESR's statement.

findings.product: Belkin UltraCharge Retractable GaN Wall Charger 67W
findings.label: Cable/port output and protocols per Belkin's FAQ
findings.value: up to 67 W to one device through either the built-in cable or the USB-C port; two devices 45 W + 20 W (65 W combined); 'Both USB-C ports support PD 3.1 and PPS' (the hardware section says PD 3.2 with PPS); AVS not mentioned; cable 3.3 ft (1 m); larger laptops 'may' charge slower
findings.source_title: Belkin Official Support - Belkin UltraCharge Retractable GaN Wall Charger 67W FAQs
findings.note: This is ChatGPT's cited page; it settles that 67 W is on the cable itself. Belkin contradicts itself on PD version within the page. With no AVS statement, it cannot be shown to meet Apple's iPhone 18 Pro requirement.
